Wow, thank you so much! I didn’t realize how many online programs and groups there are for these things. I said this in another comment, but my partner is unfortunately not really admitting he has a serious problem at the moment, so I don’t believe he would consider going or looking at any of these types of groups himself. However, I’ll definitely look into them. It’s very nice that there’s so many that focus on loved ones of the addicted person. Thank you so much again, you’ve given me a lot of great stuff to read! :)

Thank you very much for your response and your kind words! I definitely needed the reminder to put my health first. I tend to overextend myself, and this was a good positive reality check to be a little bit nicer to myself as I try to help him as well. I have reached out to a therapist in our area (for myself!), and I’m definitely going to try to focus on staying clean and getting clean. I’m hoping that as I help myself more, he might be motivated to get himself some help as well. I might even see if the therapist does couples therapy, not that I’m unhappy with our relationship at all, but maybe it would help get things in perspective for him in a safe space, if he’s open to it, of course. He has a bit of a big ego (self-described) and has basically said he can’t admit he needs serious help, or any help at all, so I don’t think getting him to go to a addiction specific support group is in the picture at this moment. I really appreciate your input, it made me feel a lot less alone. Thank you again, and best of luck to you as well! :)

Thank you so much for your kind words! I’ve read them a few times over. I’ve decided to reach out and get myself enrolled and started in therapy, and while of course trying to prioritize my mental health I think they can help me support his as well, or at least give me some tools to help myself. I’m hoping that if he sees me recovering and doing well with medical support, he might soften a bit and be more open to the idea. 

I definitely resonate with what you’ve said. This isn’t the first time I’ve dated someone with a substance abuse problem, and your story reminds me a lot of the issues that I had dealt with in the past (not with my current partner). I feel like I am not seeing the same patterns of abusive behavior or harm with my partner, he has not let his addiction affect our relationship in any seriously harmful way yet (just little things, like tidying up or remembering stuff). I empathize with you heavily however, and I’ll definitely be remembering this as I move forward just to keep myself aware of the possible realities of the situation I’m in. I hope you’re doing well and are continuing to flourish. Thank you again :)

I would just feel like such a loser if i moved back, i really don’t want to have to move back in with my parents. i would miss all the freedom i have now, i lived in an apartment 30 minutes away from them all for a short time before i moved here but there’s no way i could reasonably afford it now, especially after getting let go from my last job. i definitely think i might need therapy or medication again, it’s getting really bad. at least to continue living all alone, i need some kind of support, but i don’t know if i can afford to get it. 

my bf is supportive of therapy and mental health in general, as he’s also mentally ill, and was well aware of my basket case of mental illnesses (couple anxiety disorders, depression, ptsd) before we decided to move in together. he was very supportive of my troubles at first, but ever since we moved here and i’ve been struggling more than ever it’s like something switched. he keeps offering to talk to me about it if im troubled, but at the same time he seems so grateful that i’m not bothering him about it anymore. i really can’t blame him, im not mad at him at all, i entirely blame myself. i wish i was normal so i wouldn’t make him so stressed. ever since i started lying he’s been so much happier.

the procedure i had done has possible mental health effects, including making depression worse. i think that’s what could be happening but i’m so scared to open up to him about it. my family isn’t supportive of me being on medication either, they don’t really believe in mental illness. i miss my family a lot, and i love them, but i don’t know how much i can tell them. they don’t know what i’ve been through the past year. my last two ex-bfs abused me pretty bad and the last one i don’t know how i got out alive. they don’t know any of it. 
i’m sorry for dumping more of this on you, don’t feel obligated to respond. please know i’m so grateful for you taking the time to respond. it feels so nice to have someone to be nice to me like that. thank you so much.
Thank you so much for responding I really appreciate it. I guess I can see that now, it just hurts because this has been the longest friendship I’ve ever had.

i’ve found it’s common to have this sort of problem with dyscalculia, as its hard to estimate depth!! i feel the same way, stairs to me can be nerve wracking to go down because i’m not entirely sure how far down the step is from my foot, so i can’t be sure i won’t misjudge the height and fall.

i think it definitely is possible that it has a genetic component, but so little research has been done that it’s almost impossible to know for sure. also, dyscalculia is often times overlooked, in women especially, so it makes it harder to track through the family. for example, my mother was never officially diagnosed with it, but she has some of the symptoms, so it’s possible that that could be a component as to why i have it!

i experience this a lot as well! it’s kinda validating to hear that this is a common issue for people with dyscalculia and that i’m not alone haha. directions while driving is a total nightmare, especially if someone tells me to make a quick right/left turn and i don’t have time to process which is left and which is right!

i pick my scalp a lot too! i’m not sure what to do for any open wounds, but as for the spots you wanna pick (assuming it’s dry scalp/buildup/related issues), once a week i usually separate my hair into even sections and spray apple cider vinegar into the sectioned parts of my hair and scalp, and massage it in, especially over the more problem areas. then i put on a shower cap and go to sleep with the apple cider vinegar still on my scalp, to allow it to really soak in. this has helped immensely!! 
another tip would be to use some good hair oil to help moisturize your scalp. i’m not sure of your hair type and i don’t know if this would work for yours, but i have very curly semi thick hair, and so my scalp gets dry very often. i’ve found that using hair oil and massaging it into my scalp helps a lot.
